## Global Instructions

# fogbell

fogbell turns Alertmanager notifications into one Slack thread per incident, with buttons that act
on it, and keeps its state on the Slack message as metadata. `main` is the trunk; semantic-release tags it. Run `mise run setup` once and every tool through `mise exec --`. Start at
[docs/index.md](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/fogbell/src/branch/main/docs/index.md).

## Commits

Conventional Commits; stage only the paths you changed, never `git add -A`, `git add .` or
`git commit -a`. Sign off every commit with `git commit -s` (DCO, checked in CI). Releases are cut from
commit types by semantic-release; do not edit versions in `Chart.yaml` or anywhere else.

## Facts the tree won't tell you

- The metadata payload on Slack messages is a stored format. Its field names and the JSON-string
  encoding of nested values are schema version 1 (`internal/state`): never rename or retype a field.
  A new field is optional and absent on old messages; read it with its zero value in mind.
- `cmd/fogbell` reads flags; `internal/app` builds everything from the configuration; logic lives in
  the other `internal/` packages. A new system is an adapter on a port (`enrich.Enricher`,
  `engine.Tracker`, `investigate.Investigator`, `events.Sink`), wired in `internal/app`, never a case
  in the engine.
- No comments in Go code. Doc comments that tools read are fine.
- Every enrichment is optional and never fails an incident: the runner in `internal/engine` counts
  each outcome in `fogbell_enrichment_total{kind,result}`; an enricher returns an outcome or an error
  and never counts itself.
- The lifecycle is `engine.Decide`; a button is an entry in the action registry; time-driven work is
  a maintenance task with a due check.
- Never post, log or put a secret value in an error or a URL. Log lines posted to Slack go through
  `internal/redact` first.
- Tests fake Slack with `internal/slacktest` and every other service with `net/http/httptest`. A bug
  fix lands with a test that fails on the old code.
- Message text is part of the contract: tests assert on it. Change a sentence only on purpose.
- The project names no estate, company or person that uses it. Anything site-specific (URLs, channel
  names, label names, icons) is configuration.

## Before opening a pull request

Run `mise run verify` and put its result in the pull request.

## Decisions

Decisions go in [docs/adrs/](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/fogbell/src/branch/main/docs/adrs/README.md) (MADR 4.0, append-only, each with a
`### Confirmation`). Evidence goes in `docs/research/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`.

# webgrip baseline

These rules hold in every webgrip repository. The repository's own text outside this block wins where it disagrees.

- Secrets have a level, and OpenBao holds the only original ([homelab-cluster ADR-0055](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/homelab-cluster/src/branch/main/docs/techdocs/docs/adr/adr-0055-one-secrets-model-six-levels.md)). Never put a plaintext value in a file or add a `*.sops.yaml` outside the floor. Write the manifests and hand the person the `bao kv put` command; never handle the value. The `secrets-levels` skill places a secret and the `guard-secrets` hook enforces the floor.
- Deliver through a pull request: branch from `main`, push the branch and open the pull request. Push to `main` only where the repository's `AGENTS.md` says to; a rejected push to `main` is branch protection working, so push a branch instead. After a push, check the commit is on the remote (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/<branch>`). A forced update of a shared branch is an incident.
- Several sessions share one working tree. Commit only the paths you wrote (`git commit -- <paths>`), never `git add -A`, `git add .` or `git commit -a`, and expect any local commit to be pushed by another session at any moment ([shared working tree](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/shared-working-tree.md)).
- Run tools through mise (`mise exec -- <cmd>`); versions are pinned in `mise.toml`.
- Open a file with your file-reading tool, not `cat`, `head` or `sed` in a shell: rules scoped to a path load only when that tool reads a matching file.
- Write Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`) with an optional scope, one change per commit.
- Renovate owns dependency versions: review its pull requests instead of bumping what it manages.
- Reuse before building: generate, then reference (a pinned `uses:` or an `@webgrip` package), then sync pull requests, then a one-off copy ([reuse and releases](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/reuse-and-releases.md)).
- No comments in code. Carry intent in names, types, small functions and tests; reasoning goes to `docs/` or an ADR. Machine-read directives stay: shebangs, `# syntax=`, `# renovate:`, schema hints, `@ts-*`, `eslint-*`, `# shellcheck`, `# noqa`, `//go:*` and doc comments a tool reads ([ai-skills ADR-0001](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/ai-skills/src/branch/main/org/adrs/adr-0001-no-comments-in-code.md)).
- Docs are TechDocs (MkDocs under `docs/`) and change with the behaviour. Durable knowledge goes into the repository, skill or command that owns it, never into agent memory.
- Validate with the repository's documented gate before committing, and say plainly what failed or was skipped. Check the primary source before claiming something works or never worked.
- Keep organisations apart: no names, hosts, ids or people of an employer or client in a webgrip repository.
- The Bash tool may run zsh: quote variables, use arrays, `set -o pipefail` before gating on a pipeline, and close stdin (`< /dev/null`) for CLIs that may read it.

## Files matching `**/*.tf, **/*.tftest.hcl, **/.terraform.lock.hcl`

# OpenTofu

- Use OpenTofu (`tofu`) at the version the repository pins, never `terraform`, because the state encryption and the CI images are OpenTofu's.
- Before committing, run `tofu fmt -recursive`, then `tofu init -backend=false` and `tofu validate`, and `tofu test` where the root has tests, because CI runs the same checks without credentials on every push.
- Commit `.terraform.lock.hcl` whenever `tofu init` changes it, because CI installs exactly the providers the lock file names.
- Keep the `encryption` block `enforced = true` for both state and plan, and never rename its key provider or method, because the encrypted state embeds those names and a rename makes it unreadable.
- Leave `tofu apply` to the repository's applier (the CI job on `main`, or tofu-controller in the cluster), except for the break-glass or import path the repository documents, because an apply from a laptop or a branch skips the reviewed plan.
- Give a resource whose loss loses data or a node `prevent_destroy`, because a plan that replaces it should fail rather than apply.
- Stop managing, rename or adopt a resource with `removed {}`, `moved {}` and `import {}` blocks, because a block is reviewed in the plan and a `tofu state` command is not.
- Mark a variable or output that carries a credential `sensitive = true` and pass its value from OpenBao through `TF_VAR_*`, because a `*.tfvars` file in Git or an unmarked output prints the value in every plan.

## Files matching `**/Dockerfile*`

# Container images

- Pin the `# syntax=` frontend and every base image by tag and digest (`name:tag@sha256:<digest>`), with a `# renovate:` line above an `ARG` that holds it, because the digest makes the build reproducible and the tag is what Renovate moves.
- Verify every file a build downloads against a checksum pinned next to its version (`ADD --checksum=` or `sha256sum -c`), because a release asset can change under a fixed URL.
- Give a runtime image a non-root `USER`, because the clusters' pod security policies refuse or report a container that runs as root.
- Keep build-only tools in an earlier stage and copy only the artefacts into the final one, because every extra package in the final image is attack surface the CVE gate counts.

## Files matching `**/kubernetes/**`

# Kubernetes and Flux

## GitOps

- Change a manifest or values file instead of running `kubectl apply/patch/delete` or `helm install/upgrade`, because Flux reconciles Git and reverts or fights anything applied by hand; reading the cluster is fine.
- Call a rollout live only once the Flux revision it reconciled and the running image digest both match the commit, because a merged manifest or a green pipeline is not a running resource.
- Express order between applications with `dependsOn` on the Flux Kustomization or HelmRelease, because Flux applies independent Kustomizations in parallel.
- Annotate an object whose deletion takes the cluster or its data down (Flux itself, the CNI, a namespace holding volumes) with `kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/prune: disabled`, because moving or deleting its file would otherwise uninstall it.
- Escape a runtime shell variable in a manifest under a Kustomization with `postBuild` substitution as `$${VAR}`, because Flux substitutes every `${...}` before the container sees it.
- Annotate a generated ConfigMap whose file payload contains `$` text with `kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/substitute: disabled` instead of escaping it, because envsubst fails the whole build on an unbalanced brace.
- Template a private hostname or address through the substitution variables the repository defines, because the literal values are kept out of Git.

## Charts in HelmReleases

- Pin an `OCIRepository` `ref` to a tag and its digest, and a `HelmRepository` chart to an exact version, because Renovate moves both and a floating reference deploys a chart nobody reviewed.
- Give every HelmRelease install and upgrade remediation with retries, because a failed release otherwise stays failed until someone intervenes.
- Deploy a workload that has no chart of its own through the bjw-s `app-template` chart, because `application-template` and `common-charts` are archived ([homelab-cluster ADR-0078](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/homelab-cluster/src/branch/main/docs/techdocs/docs/adr/adr-0078-one-release-recipe-four-kinds.md)).

## Workloads

- Reference every container image as `tag@sha256:<digest>`, because the clusters' admission policies refuse or report a mutable reference.
- Run containers with `runAsNonRoot`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, all capabilities dropped and the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile, because the pod security policies refuse or flag anything less.
- Set CPU and memory requests and a memory limit on every container, because the clusters' admission policies refuse or report a container without them.
- Place a workload by the `node.webgrip.io/pool` label, never by hostname or the control-plane role, because pools are how nodes are grouped and nodes come and go.
- Give a workload in a default-deny namespace its own policy that allows only the flows it needs, because everything else is dropped silently.

## Files matching `**/talos/**`

# Talos

- Keep the Talos and Kubernetes versions in `talos/talenv.yaml` under their `# renovate:` lines, because the config generator, the node image build and Renovate all read them there.
- Change `configContract` only as a planned migration, separate from a `talosVersion` bump, because it fixes the shape of the generated machine config documents and existing patches can collide with the new shape.
- Add or remove a system extension in the Image Factory schematic, never in a machine config patch, because extensions ship in the installer image the schematic names.
- Apply machine config through the repository's path (its `just talos-*` recipe or the OpenTofu apply), never a hand `talosctl apply-config`, because a hand apply drifts from Git and can reboot a control plane.

## Files matching `.forgejo/**`

# Forgejo Actions

- Reference a reusable workflow in shorthand, pinned to a SHA: `uses: webgrip/workflows/.forgejo/workflows/<name>.yml@<sha> # vX.Y.Z`. A full `https://` URL leaves the job waiting forever for runner labels.
- An `if:` on a `uses:` job does nothing: Forgejo v15 flattens the called jobs and drops it. Gate inside the reusable workflow (`only-refs`, `enabled`) or give the calling job its own `runs-on`.
- Use `runs-on: docker`, the `Europe/Amsterdam` timezone (cron schedules too) and `@webgrip/semantic-release-config` for releases.
- Check that a GitHub Marketplace action works on forgejo-runner before proposing it ([Forgejo CI](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/forgejo-ci.md)).
